name: DVWA v3 detection method on OWASP Juice Shop, against scanner-generated attacks including families never tested before
registered: 2026-11-26, before any Juice Shop traffic was generated and before any detector was fitted on it
question: Does the v3 method (per-field request profiles, host novelty, response shift and a learned forest, fused by Fisher's method over benign-calibrated tail probabilities), learned only from benign Juice Shop traffic, detect attacks generated by independent tools, including attack families absent from the DVWA lab, at a low benign alert rate?
application: OWASP Juice Shop v19.2.1 (tag commit f87c6f58c49b61c9de20e4d69a9bdb1fbd4f3bd3, MIT license), the official node22 linux x64 release archive, run on loopback under strace (execve, connect, openat).
telemetry: A serializing proxy (serial_proxy.py) gives each source its own port (benign 9001, attack 9002), forwards one request at a time and records every exchange; system calls are joined to the request in flight. ZAP's X-ZAP-Scan-ID header is recorded as the label and removed before forwarding, so neither the application nor the detector sees it.
method_carried_over: Imported unchanged from experiment-b/dvwa-correlation-v3/model_v3.py and the DVWA lab: request_profiles, response_profiles, evidence, fused, lab.features, lab.build_vocab. New code only turns proxy records into request rows: numeric and identifier-like path segments become N and X; query parameters and flattened JSON body fields are the fields. Splits 40/35/25, 0.5% budget, IsolationForest(n_estimators=300, random_state=2026112901).
development: One session of 3000 benign requests from benign.py (seed 2026112902): catalogue browsing and search, reviews, registration and login, basket, order tracking, feedback. Benign only; frozen by hash.
test: One fresh session after the freeze. benign.py (seed 2026112903) runs throughout on port 9001. On port 9002: ZAP (zaproxy/zap-stable, digest recorded) is seeded by one pass of benign.py through it, then its active scan runs with default policy for at most 25 minutes; then sqlmap runs against the product search parameter and the login JSON body, at most 15 minutes each.
labels: benign = port 9001. attack attempt = port 9002 with a ZAP plugin id, or with sqlmap's user agent. Everything else on port 9002 (seeding, crawl) is UNKNOWN and excluded, never counted as benign. Confirmed attack = a request named as evidence by a ZAP alert of Medium or High risk (same plugin, same path, alert attack string present in the request). Families: ZAP scanner names containing 'SQL Injection', 'Command Injection' or 'Remote OS', 'Path Traversal' or 'File Inclusion', and all sqlmap requests, are families seen in the DVWA lab; every other scanner is an unseen family.
pass_condition: For the fused detector: (1) at most 1% of benign test requests alert; (2) at least 90% of confirmed attack requests alert. If fewer than 30 confirmed attack requests exist, the outcome is inconclusive, not a pass. Reported beside it, not as criteria: detection of all attack attempts, by family and seen versus unseen, and each component alone.
harness_checks: A smoke stage, run before development with no detector code executed, checks that labels, plugin ids and the system-call join work. The test aborts if no request carries a ZAP plugin id.
known_limits: Benign traffic is generated by benign.py, not real users. Scanner attack attempts include many probes that would not succeed; the confirmed subset depends on what ZAP can confirm. Duplicate parameter names collapse to one field.
not_claimed: Production false-alarm rates; attacks by a human adversary.
